# Bucker fluid waveguide, 100 Hz: transmission loss from a wavenumber-integration solution.
# 
# Problem: Jensen, Kuperman, Porter & Schmidt, Computational Ocean Acoustics, 2nd ed.,
# Sect. 4.10.2, Figs. 4.17-4.18 (proposed by Bucker as a benchmark; COA cites Lee & McDaniel,
# Comp. Math. Appl. 14, 305-423, 1987). Water 240 m deep, sound speed 1500 m/s at the
# surface, 1498 m/s at 120 m and 1500 m/s at 240 m, linear between, density 1.0; fluid
# half-space 1505 m/s, density 2.1, no attenuation. Source 30 m, receiver 90 m. The values
# are those of the OASES test deck tloss/bucker.dat. COA's point: the weak speed contrast
# traps few modes while the density contrast puts much of the field in the continuous
# spectrum, so a sum over the trapped modes alone is wrong even at long range.
# 
# Solution: the Acoustics Toolbox's SCOOTER (wavenumber integration, exact for this
# range-independent problem up to discretisation) run through uacpy as
# Scooter(c_high=1e9), i.e. integrating from k = 0. Cross-checked against OASES OAST run
# through uacpy at its defaults: 0.006 dB median and 0.03 dB 90th-percentile |dTL| over
# 2-20 km, 0.03 dB median over 0.1-2 km.
# 
# TL is dB re 1 m.
# 
# range_km  TL_90m_dB
